Natural pain relief, made in Aotearoa.

X-ZONE is a family of herbal rubs, sprays and roll-ons built on eleven native New Zealand healing herbs. The brand should feel like where it comes from: the bush, the water, real people who move.

Move Freely. Live Naturally.

The brand line, in the client's own words. Short form: "Move Freely, Naturally." "11 NZ healing herbs" is the supporting proof point and may sit beneath it.

Personality: authentic, trustworthy, empowering, informative, generous. Never clinical, never hype.

01 Logo

Primary: green on white
Reversed: white on green or black, or on a photo with a dark wash
Icon: the koru X, used alone for avatars and favicons
  • Clear space all round equals the height of the X.
  • Minimum width 30 mm in print, 120 px on screen. Below that, use the icon.
  • Social avatar is the icon in black on a white circle, no ring.
  • The icon may be used as a watermark at 8 to 12% opacity on green.
  • Never recolour, outline, add a shadow, or stretch.
  • Never place on a busy photo without the dark wash behind it.

Green is the brand and white gives it air. Each range has its own pair, taken from X-ZONE's own brand page: Relief is green with lime, Joints is navy with orange, Sports is black with red. Use one range's pair per layout and let the accent point at one thing: a subline, a number, a pill. Lime and orange are never used for small text on white.

03 Typography

Why rub it in,
not just rub it on
Galano Grotesque Bold for sublines and names

Galano Grotesque Medium or Light for body copy, captions and anything longer than two lines. In Canva and on the web, Poppins stands in for every weight. Keep lines to about 65 characters.

Bold, spaced, for labels
DisplayGalano Grotesque Black (Poppins ExtraBold in Canva and web), sentence case, tight leading (1.05). Headlines ask a question or state one fact. BodyGalano Grotesque Medium / Light (Poppins Regular / Light), 1.45 leading. Bold for emphasis, never italic. Subheadings in Galano Grotesque Bold (Poppins Bold). LabelsGalano Grotesque Bold (Poppins Bold), uppercase, 1.6 pt tracking, 7 to 8 pt. FallbackArial in email signatures and Office documents, where web fonts will not load. CaseSentence case everywhere. ALL CAPS only for short labels, never for headlines or taglines.

04 Photography

PlaceNZ bush, water, light through canopy
PeopleJess, Dan, customers, athletes. Real, not stock
ProductIn the hand or in use, never floating
  • Natural light, green and earth tones, nothing colour-graded warm or blue.
  • When text sits on a photo, apply a dark wash in the range's colour at 15% top to 75% bottom.
  • Show the body part the product is for: ankle, knee, shoulder, hands.
  • No gym stock imagery, no white studio backgrounds, no AI-generated people.

05 Voice

Sound like this

  • Teach first. Explain why the herb works, what the bruise colour means, what to do in the first 48 hours.
  • We, not I. Plain and warm, short sentences, NZ spelling. Kiwi, not corporate.
  • Te reo greetings are part of the voice: Kia ora, Ngā mihi, Aotearoa.
  • Name the eleven herbs. Let customers say "the only one that works for me".
  • Humour rarely, and never political or sexual. Slang only where it fits.

Not like this

  • No miracle claims. "Supports", "helps", "traditionally used", never "cures".
  • No price-only posts, ever. A special sits inside something useful.
  • No exclamation marks in headlines. No emoji anywhere. Hashtags are fine.
  • Never knock a competitor by name. A general pharma contrast is fine.
  • No "clinically proven" unless the independent test is linked.

The 80/20 rule. Four in five posts educate: herb science, injury first aid, wellness. One in five sells, and even that one is anchored in a reason to use the product.

06 Instagram system

SPORTS
Why rub it in,
not just rub it onThe science of massage plus herbs
@XZONENZ · XZONE.NZ
Rolled your ankle?The first 48 hours, step by step
Range-ground post (top, Sports shown) and photo-led post (bottom). Alternate them down the grid.
  1. Avatar. Black koru X on a white circle. Never the full logo.
  2. Range-ground post. Bush photo under a dark wash in the range's colour, white logo top left, accent pill top right, Poppins ExtraBold headline bottom left with an accent subline, footer strip with handle and site.
  3. Photo-led post. Real photo full bleed, title band across the top in the range's ground colour: white headline, accent subline. Nothing else on the image.
  4. Grid rhythm. Alternate range-ground and photo-led so the grid reads as one brand at a glance. Same logo position, same font, same range colours, every time.
  5. Reels. Shot like a film, not a slideshow: slow camera moves, cross-dissolves, grain, a few words on screen, no voiceover unless it is Jess or Dan. Cover frame follows the range-ground post.
  6. Captions. First line is the lesson. Product mention last. Hashtags: five at most, Aotearoa and herb names before generic pain tags.
